## Your agent (one per person)

Opened in one terminal tab, with `/remote-control` on so the human can check in from their phone. It works through both of its person's folders, one task at a time.

Work on one task at a time in my folders: plan it, show me the plan before writing code, build it, prove it works, commit, and post on the board when a teammate depends on it. Start with my next unchecked step in BUILD.md. Check the board with `tools/board unread` before each new task.

For each task, give it a brief like this:

> Build: [the feature, in 2-3 sentences] in [folder]/. Read [folder]/README.md first. Follow the "[section]" part of CONTRACTS.md. Done means: [what should work], it runs without errors, and you've committed. Check it by: [running the tests / opening the page and taking a screenshot]. Then give me your summary (see CLAUDE.md).

## A second agent (only when it's worth it)

Open a second tab only when two tasks can really run at the same time, for example something long-running (the fine-tune, a head build, a batch of test conversations) while you work on something else. Give it the same brief format, keep it to a different folder from your first agent (or a separate `git worktree`), and close it when that task is done.

## Saving credits

- Run `/clear` between unrelated tasks, so the agent isn't re-reading a long old conversation with every message.

269:## Part 5: MLH Best Use of Entire
270-
271:### Uncle for the Entire track
272-
273:Three people built Uncle over 36 hours by directing Claude Code agents in parallel — one per person, working on separate folders of the same repo. Entire captures every agent session (38 checkpoints across 2 sessions), indexes the codebase into a searchable graph (123 files, 694 symbols), distills decisions into Brain (7 facts extracted from sessions plus 2 authored), and tracks feature work through Trails (3 active trails linked to branches).
274-
275:The MLH Entire track asks teams to use Entire's Sessions, Graph and Brain to create seamless human-AI collaboration, keep a clean code history, and show measurable token efficiency.
276-
277:### How Uncle uses Entire
278-
279:| Entire capability | What we did | Proof | Where to look |
280-| --- | --- | --- | --- |
281:| Sessions | Every agent session captured automatically; 38 checkpoints across 2 sessions, covering the full build from skeleton to fine-tuned model | 38 checkpoints, 152 exchanges indexed | `entire activity`, `entire session list` |
282:| Graph | Codebase indexed with 123 files and 694 symbols; agents search commits and sessions semantically with `entire search` instead of reading files blindly | `entire search "placeholder system"` returns the relevant commits and session snippets | `entire search`, `entire graph` |
283:| Brain | Key decisions distilled from sessions and authored as durable facts: the placeholder guarantee, grounding test results, the rejected equal-income fix | 7 distilled facts + 2 authored facts; 1,138 history records | `entire brain recall`, `entire brain stats` |
284:| Trails | Feature work tracked in 3 trails linked to branches: fine-tune model, Monte Carlo sim, grounding test | Trail #4, #5, #6 on `entire trail list` | `entire trail list --project gh/e-yang6` |
285-
286-### Challenges we ran into
287-
288:Coordinating three agents working on the same repo at the same time. Each person owns separate folders (sim/, voice/, head/, xr/), but the parts connect through shared contracts (CONTRACTS.md). When one agent changed how the simulation outputs its facts sheet, the voice agent needed to update how it reads those values. The pinned GitHub issue ("Message Board") and Entire's shared session context helped, but the real coordination came from the contracts file and strict folder ownership.
289-
290:Getting agents to stay in their lanes. Each agent is told which folders it owns and which it must not edit. Without this discipline, two agents editing the same file would create merge conflicts. Entire's session capture means a human can review what each agent did and resume where it left off after a sleep shift.
291-
292:Brain distillation surfacing real decisions. After running `entire brain distill`, Brain extracted facts like the rejected equal-retirement-income fix (the equality was a valid consequence of deterministic target spending, not a bug) directly from the session transcripts. These facts persist across sessions so future agents do not re-investigate closed decisions.
293-
294-### Limits and next steps
--

# xr/: the WebXR app in the headset

Owner: Person 3. Spec: PLAN.md Part 3 (showing it). Follow DESIGN-RULES.md.

Lives here: the three.js WebXR app for the Meta Quest browser with passthrough, the mirror frame, loading a head, opening the mouth and driving it from the audio, blinking and small head movements, blending aged skin versions, the sliders with hand tracking (controllers as backup), and the theme file from the design rounds.

## Running it

- Open `/xr/` on the live link (once the server serves it) or locally: from the repo root, `python3 -m http.server 8123`, then http://127.0.0.1:8123/xr/.
- Quest browser: "Start in the headset" enters passthrough AR; the mirror appears about 1 m in front of where you're looking.
- Laptop: "Start" plays in the page (for casting and screenshots).
- `?head=<name>` loads `/head/builds/<name>/head.glb` (CONTRACTS.md). Without it, a stand-in head loads from the three.js sample files (dev only; its licence isn't confirmed, so it's never committed or shown to judges as ours).
- `?voice=live` uses the `/voice` socket (CONTRACTS.md) and the microphone (Jeffrey's `/mic.js`, started after Start; the browser asks for permission). Default is `sample/greeting.json`, a Mac `say` line packed as contract reply messages. Rebuild it with `xr/sample/make-sample.sh`.
- Tests: `node --test xr/` (mouth analysis, PCM decoding, the queue start-time rule).

## Files

- `mouth.js`: audio frame -> jaw / wide / round (loudness and zero-crossing rate), plus smoothing.
- `pcm.js`: base64 16-bit PCM -> floats. `player.js`: gapless Web Audio queue with an analyser.
- `voice.js`: sample and live sources of contract messages. `head.js`: loading a head, blend shapes, blinking and sway.
- `main.js`, `index.html`, `theme.css`: the scene, mirror frame, Start button and caption (DESIGN-RULES.md).
# head/: building and aging the 3D head

Owner: Person 3. Spec: PLAN.md Part 3 (building and aging). Contracts: head files out (CONTRACTS.md).

Lives here: frame picking and MediaPipe segmentation, COLMAP camera recovery, landmark triangulation, fitting the MakeHuman head template and hair shape, painting the texture, the face-aging step (run on the Vultr GPU), grey hair, age shape changes, the prepared aged skin versions, and saving finished heads.

Based on [Punching Face](https://github.com/akashngb/punching-face). People's videos and heads stay out of git (.gitignore).

## Blend shapes the XR app drives

Every `head.glb` needs these morph targets (names exact): `jawOpen`, `mouthWide`, `mouthRound`, `eyeBlink_L`, `eyeBlink_R`. ARKit names (`mouthStretch_L/R`, `mouthFunnel`) also work. See `xr/head.js`.

## Building a head

One time: `bash head/setup.sh` (Homebrew Python 3.11, packages in `head/.venv`, the CC0 MakeHuman template and MediaPipe models in `head/models/`; none of it goes in git).

Film: a phone on a stand at head height, about 1 m away, even light. The person starts facing the camera with a neutral face, turns slowly all the way round (about 20 seconds), and ends facing the camera again. Keep the mouth closed. Use the original file from the phone (AirDrop "Options > All Photos Data" or a cable), not one shrunk by a chat app.

Build: `head/build.sh captures/<video> <name>` writes `head/builds/<name>/head.glb` and `report.json`, then open `/xr/?head=<name>`. About 100 s on an M5 Mac.

| Message | What to do |
|---|---|
| Only N usable views / Only N views show the face | Film again: slower, the whole turn, start and end facing the camera |
| Only N frames could be placed | Film again in even light, closer, turning slowly |
| Face points don't line up between frames | Film again with a still, neutral face |

How it works (PLAN.md Part 3, following Punching Face's method): MediaPipe masks and face landmarks per frame, COLMAP cameras (exhaustive matching closes the loop of the turn), landmarks triangulated with a held-out check, the template warped onto them (thin-plate RBF), the scalp pushed out to the outlines for hair, a texture baked from about 40 views, and the five mouth and eye shapes from MakeHuman's CC0 expression units carried through the same warp. Tests: `head/.venv/bin/pytest head/tests` (from `head/`: `.venv/bin/pytest`).

1	"""Steps 4 to 7: fit the template, fit hair, bake the texture, rig, export head.glb.
2	
3	CLI: python -m uncle_head.assemble <work> <out_dir>   (writes out_dir/head.glb, assemble.json)
4	"""
5	from __future__ import annotations
6	
7	import json
8	import sys
9	import time
10	from pathlib import Path
11	
12	import numpy as np
13	from scipy.spatial import cKDTree
14	
15	from .export import export_glb
16	from .fit import anchor_positions, warp_template
17	from .hair import fit_hair
18	from .rig import build_morphs, mouth_interior
19	from .template import load_head_template, vertex_normals, weld
20	from .texture import bake_texture
21	from .views import head_views
22	
23	HEAD = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
24	MODELS = HEAD / "models"
25	ANCHORS = HEAD / "template" / "anchors.json"
26	TEXTURE_VIEWS = 40
27	TEXTURE_SIZE = 2048
28	HAIR_MAX_OUT = 0.06
29	TEETH, TONGUE, MOUTH = (222, 216, 204), (140, 70, 66), (34, 22, 20)
30	SCLERA, IRIS, PUPIL = (226, 221, 212), (78, 56, 42), (22, 17, 14)
31	
32	
33	def _hair_weight(verts, faces, face_anchors):
34	    """0 on the face, rising to 1 from 2 to 5 cm away from any face landmark."""
35	    d, _ = cKDTree(face_anchors).query(verts)
36	    w = np.clip((d - 0.02) / 0.03, 0, 1)
37	    w = w * w * (3 - 2 * w)
38	    used = np.zeros(len(verts), bool)
39	    used[np.unique(faces)] = True
40	    return np.where(used, w, 0.0)
41	
42	
43	def _eye_colours(verts):
44	    c = verts.mean(0)
45	    d = verts - c
46	    d /= np.linalg.norm(d, axis=1, keepdims=True) + 1e-12
47	    out = np.tile(SCLERA, (len(verts), 1)).astype(float)
48	    out[d[:, 2] > np.cos(np.radians(26))] = IRIS
49	    out[d[:, 2] > np.cos(np.radians(11))] = PUPIL
50	    return out
51	
52	
53	def _subset(verts, faces, uvs, face_idx, morphs=None):
54	    f = faces[face_idx]
55	    used, inv = np.unique(f, return_inverse=True)
56	    part = {"verts": verts[used], "faces": inv.reshape(-1, 3), "uvs": uvs[used]}
57	    if morphs is not None:
58	        part["morphs"] = {k: m[used] for k, m in morphs.items()}
59	    return part
60	
61	
62	def run(work, out_dir) -> dict:
63	    work, out_dir = Path(work), Path(out_dir)
64	    timings = {}
65	    t0 = time.time()
66	    template = load_head_template(MODELS)
67	    anchors = json.loads(ANCHORS.read_text())
68	    points = np.array(json.loads((work / "landmarks3d.json").read_text())["points"])
69	    verts, warp = warp_template(template, anchors, points[anchors["landmark"]])
70	    timings["fit_s"] = time.time() - t0
71	
72	    t0 = time.time()
73	    views = head_views(work)
74	    skin = template.parts["skin"]
75	    wv, wf, inv = weld(verts, template.faces[skin], template.source_index)
76	    weight = _hair_weight(wv, wf, anchor_positions(verts, template.faces, anchors))
77	    verts = fit_hair(wv, vertex_normals(wv, wf), weight, views, max_out=HAIR_MAX_OUT, faces=wf)[inv]
78	    timings["hair_s"] = time.time() - t0
79	
80	    t0 = time.time()
81	    interior = mouth_interior(template, verts)
82	    outer_skin = np.setdiff1d(skin, interior)
83	    front = min(range(len(views)), key=lambda i: abs(views[i]["yaw"]) if views[i]["yaw"] is not None else 1e9)
84	    pick = sorted(set(np.linspace(0, len(views) - 1, TEXTURE_VIEWS).astype(int).tolist()) | {front})
85	    texture, tex_report = bake_texture(verts, template.faces[skin], template.uvs, [views[i] for i in pick], size=TEXTURE_SIZE, occluders=(verts, template.faces))
86	    timings["texture_s"] = time.time() - t0
87	
88	    t0 = time.time()
89	    morphs = build_morphs(template, warp, MODELS)
90	    parts = [{"name": "skin", "texture": texture, **_subset(verts, template.faces, template.uvs, outer_skin, morphs)}]
91	    parts.append({"name": "mouth", "color": MOUTH, **_subset(verts, template.faces, template.uvs, interior, morphs)})
92	    parts.append({"name": "teeth", "color": TEETH, **_subset(verts, template.faces, template.uvs, template.parts["teeth"], morphs)})
93	    parts.append({"name": "tongue", "color": TONGUE, **_subset(verts, template.faces, template.uvs, template.parts["tongue"], morphs)})
94	    for eye in ("eye_l", "eye_r"):
95	        p = _subset(verts, template.faces, template.uvs, template.parts[eye], morphs)
96	        parts.append({"name": eye, "color": (255, 255, 255), "vertex_colors": _eye_colours(p["verts"]), **p})
97	    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
98	    export_glb(out_dir / "head.glb", parts)
99	    timings["rig_export_s"] = time.time() - t0
100	
101	    report = {**timings, "texture": tex_report, "texture_views": len(pick), "glb_bytes": (out_dir / "head.glb").stat().st_size}
102	    (work / "assemble.json").write_text(json.dumps(report))
103	    return report
104	
105

107	    r = run(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2])
108	    print(f"assemble: head.glb {r['glb_bytes'] / 1e6:.1f} MB; texture {r['texture']['seen_pct']:.0f}% seen from {r['texture_views']} views")

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from scipy.spatial import cKDTree

from .export import export_glb
from .fit import anchor_positions, warp_template
from .hair import fit_hair
from .rig import build_morphs, mouth_interior
from .template import load_head_template, vertex_normals, weld
from .texture import bake_texture
from .views import head_views

HEAD = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
MODELS = HEAD / "models"
ANCHORS = HEAD / "template" / "anchors.json"
TEXTURE_VIEWS = 40
TEXTURE_SIZE = 2048
HAIR_MAX_OUT = 0.06
TEETH, TONGUE, MOUTH = (222, 216, 204), (140, 70, 66), (34, 22, 20)
SCLERA, IRIS, PUPIL = (226, 221, 212), (78, 56, 42), (22, 17, 14)


def _hair_weight(verts, faces, face_anchors):
    """0 on the face, rising to 1 from 2 to 5 cm away from any face landmark."""
    d, _ = cKDTree(face_anchors).query(verts)
    w = np.clip((d - 0.02) / 0.03, 0, 1)
    w = w * w * (3 - 2 * w)
    used = np.zeros(len(verts), bool)
    used[np.unique(faces)] = True
    return np.where(used, w, 0.0)


def _eye_colours(verts):
    c = verts.mean(0)
    d = verts - c
    d /= np.linalg.norm(d, axis=1, keepdims=True) + 1e-12
    out = np.tile(SCLERA, (len(verts), 1)).astype(float)
    out[d[:, 2] > np.cos(np.radians(26))] = IRIS
    out[d[:, 2] > np.cos(np.radians(11))] = PUPIL
    return out


def _subset(verts, faces, uvs, face_idx, morphs=None):
    f = faces[face_idx]
    used, inv = np.unique(f, return_inverse=True)
    part = {"verts": verts[used], "faces": inv.reshape(-1, 3), "uvs": uvs[used]}
    if morphs is not None:
        part["morphs"] = {k: m[used] for k, m in morphs.items()}
    return part


def run(work, out_dir) -> dict:
    work, out_dir = Path(work), Path(out_dir)
    timings = {}
    t0 = time.time()
    template = load_head_template(MODELS)
    anchors = json.loads(ANCHORS.read_text())
    points = np.array(json.loads((work / "landmarks3d.json").read_text())["points"])
    verts, warp = warp_template(template, anchors, points[anchors["landmark"]])
    timings["fit_s"] = time.time() - t0

    t0 = time.time()
    views = head_views(work)
    skin = template.parts["skin"]
    wv, wf, inv = weld(verts, template.faces[skin], template.source_index)
    weight = _hair_weight(wv, wf, anchor_positions(verts, template.faces, anchors))
    verts = fit_hair(wv, vertex_normals(wv, wf), weight, views, max_out=HAIR_MAX_OUT, faces=wf)[inv]
    timings["hair_s"] = time.time() - t0

    t0 = time.time()
    interior = mouth_interior(template, verts)
    outer_skin = np.setdiff1d(skin, interior)
    front = min(range(len(views)), key=lambda i: abs(views[i]["yaw"]) if views[i]["yaw"] is not None else 1e9)
    pick = sorted(set(np.linspace(0, len(views) - 1, TEXTURE_VIEWS).astype(int).tolist()) | {front})
    texture, tex_report = bake_texture(verts, template.faces[skin], template.uvs, [views[i] for i in pick], size=TEXTURE_SIZE, occluders=(verts, template.faces))
    timings["texture_s"] = time.time() - t0

    t0 = time.time()
    morphs = build_morphs(template, warp, MODELS)
    parts = [{"name": "skin", "texture": texture, **_subset(verts, template.faces, template.uvs, outer_skin, morphs)}]
    parts.append({"name": "mouth", "color": MOUTH, **_subset(verts, template.faces, template.uvs, interior, morphs)})
    parts.append({"name": "teeth", "color": TEETH, **_subset(verts, template.faces, template.uvs, template.parts["teeth"], morphs)})
    parts.append({"name": "tongue", "color": TONGUE, **_subset(verts, template.faces, template.uvs, template.parts["tongue"], morphs)})
    for eye in ("eye_l", "eye_r"):
        p = _subset(verts, template.faces, template.uvs, template.parts[eye], morphs)
        parts.append({"name": eye, "color": (255, 255, 255), "vertex_colors": _eye_colours(p["verts"]), **p})
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    export_glb(out_dir / "head.glb", parts)
    timings["rig_export_s"] = time.time() - t0

    report = {**timings, "texture": tex_report, "texture_views": len(pick), "glb_bytes": (out_dir / "head.glb").stat().st_size}
    (work / "assemble.json").write_text(json.dumps(report))
    return report


if __name__ == "__main__":
    r = run(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2])
    print(f"assemble: head.glb {r['glb_bytes'] / 1e6:.1f} MB; texture {r['texture']['seen_pct']:.0f}% seen from {r['texture_views']} views")

The scan doesn't capture your eyes at all. The eyeballs are stand-ins from the template, coloured with three flat colours (white, brown, black). That's most of the creepiness, and the rest of the face holds up well.

## What I looked at
I rendered your saved head (`isaac.glb` from the live site) in Playwright from the front, at three-quarters, in eye close-ups, and on the live `/xr/?head=isaac` page. In the headset framing, your eyes read as **bright white rings with tiny dark dots**, which is the classic startled stare.

## How the eyes are made now
- **Nothing from the video is used for the eyes.** MediaPipe does find 10 iris points per frame, but `head/uncle_head/anchors.py:61` throws them away and keeps only the 468 face points.
- **The eyeballs are the template's eye meshes, with only 80 vertices each.** They get bent along with the face fitting, then painted by angle in `_eye_colours` (`head/uncle_head/assemble.py:43`).

## Why they look unsettling, worst first
